newsitem.title: JAPAN: Foreigners' yen bond buying due to forex - source.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners' yen bond buying due to forex - source.

text.p: The sharp rise in yen bond purchases by foreign investors in April may have been due to speculation that the yen would rise against the dollar, a bond market source said on Tuesday.

"Although it is hard to say for sure, foreigners may have tried to take advantage of fluctuations in the foreign exchange markets, and moved to buy yen...to invest in Treasury Bills (T-bills) with such funds," the source said.
It was also difficult to say for certain, however, whether their aggressive buying of yen bonds was based on a view that the yen would rise sharply against the dollar, the source said.
"If they were (betting that the yen would rise), they were right," he said.
After rising as high as 127.47 yen on May 1, the dollar tumbled more than 15 yen in a little over two weeks to hit a low of 111.98 in Tokyo trade on Tuesday.
Foreign investors primarily bought T-bills and Financing Bills (FBs), the source said.
Earlier, the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) said foreign investors' net purchases of yen bonds in April totalled a record high of 5.1777 trillion yen.
The previous high was 3.1288 trillion yen in October 1996, the JSDA said.
The figures include Japanese government bonds, notes and Treasury bills, financing bills, corporate bonds and bank debentures.
